set.body:
Observed at intaglio 8bef37e (plsneuro closure, events raster for plsneuro PD4 bd-01M3SZ0V89FTAM4Q07QY3FAPBT in the plsneuro store).

Reproduction through the public DSL
1. `plot(rows).aes(_.x, _.y).geomSegment(_.xEnd, _.yEnd).scaleYContinuous(name = "row", transform = t)`
   The render plan fails with MixedPositionScaling("x") or ("y"): "aesthetic 'y' is scaled in some layers and unscaled in others". The only data layer is the segment. Moving the scale call before or after the geom makes no difference.
2. `plot(rows).aes(_.x, _.y).scaleYContinuous(transform = Transform(..., breaks = custom, labeler = custom)).geomTile(w, h)`
   This renders, but the y axis uses default pretty breaks and labels over the raw range (0, 0.5, 1). The custom breaks and labeler are ignored. As far as the output shows, the tile layer is trained unscaled, so the plot's y scale is never registered for the axis.

Expected
An explicit continuous position scale applies to every position aesthetic of every layer that inherits the plot mapping: x/xEnd, y/yEnd, and tile centres with their extents. Otherwise the builder should reject the combination with a message naming the unsupported geom/aesthetic.

Consumer workaround (plsneuro fce9f2d, EventRaster.scala)
- Leave positions unscaled.
- Supply a `GuidePolicy.Derived(overrides = Vector(GuideSpec.Axis(AxisSide.Left, breaks, labeler)))`.
- Use geomTile, because geomSegment with any explicit scale fails.

Acceptance
- A law/regression test for segment and tile layers under an explicit transformed scale: rendered positions equal those of geomPoint at the same coordinates, and axis ticks come from the scale's breaks and labeler.
- A consumer-shaped test: a categorical-row raster (tiles at integer rows with a custom labeler) renders labelled rows without guide overrides.
set.title: Explicit position scales do not reach geomSegment/geomTile end and centre coordinates
